tools.name: intent_gate

tools.description: Adaptive dense + lexical + optional graph retrieval. A hit may carry `entity_match`, a derived display-only inference that the query text mentions one of the hit's `entities[]` names under the documented containment rule; it is not a verification result, not a span-verified fact, and not a ranking signal. Each hit's `scores.age_factor` is the retention factor applied to `scores.final`: a pure number derived from timestamps and constants, in the bank's `[retention_floor, 1]` range (exactly `1` when the curve is off), and never null for a returned hit. Each hit's `scores.trust_factor` is the trust multiplier applied to `scores.final` at the shaping site: a finite number in `[the smallest configured trust ratio, 1.0]`, always present, that only reorders hits and never changes `category`, `epistemic_kind`, or `confidence`; it is not a confidence value. A hit may also carry `exact_render`, a bounded rendering of its authoritative half: it is content, it is absent unless the request asks for it, and it never substitutes for the `get_snapshot` read of the exact stored value.

bank.description: Isolation key; overrides the connection default when present.

entity_summary.description: Return a top-level `entity_summary` object mapping each entity name present on the returned page to the number of returned hits carrying it, with name-ascending keys (default false, so the key is absent unless requested). It is counted from the returned hits' own `entities[]` and never involves new extraction. Rejected together with `include_entities: false`, because a summary is made of names. Like `hits[].entities`, it never reaches `warnings`, the `explain` trace, telemetry, or the health surfaces.

include_entities.description: Publish each hit's `entities[]` names (default true). When false, every hit's `entities` serializes as an empty array, the derived `entity_match` flag is absent, and no entity summary is built, so no entity name appears anywhere in the response. Entity names are content: they never reach `warnings`, the `explain` trace, telemetry, or the health surfaces.

include_exact.description: Attach a bounded rendering of each hit's authoritative half as `hits[].exact_render` (default false, so the key is absent from every hit unless requested). The rendering is the hit's stored snapshot serialized whole, which makes it content: like `gist`, it never reaches `warnings`, the `explain` trace, telemetry, or the health surfaces. It is bounded and never truncated: a snapshot whose rendering would exceed 512 bytes yields no rendering for that hit at all, so the field is never a prefix of a snapshot that reads as the stored value. Its token cost is an upper bound rather than an equality: a rendering of at most that many bytes is at most 128 tokens under the same heuristic `budget_tokens` uses, which counts characters rather than bytes, so a rendering within three characters of that byte count reaches that figure even when the text holds multi-byte characters, and only a rendering of fewer characters lands below it. A request that omits the toggle produces no rendering, so nothing changes for a caller who does not ask. It is a rendering and not the stored half: read `get_snapshot` for the exact value, because this field never replaces that read.

min_scores.description: Optional per-stage score floors. Every floor is inclusive (>=) and an absent or null object imposes no floor at all. Only the four names below are accepted: an unrecognised name is rejected as invalid_argument rather than read as no floor, so a mistyped floor can never return an unfiltered page. `semantic` and `keyword` are arm-local: each prunes only the arm it names, before fusion, so the other arm's candidates are unaffected and a survivor of the other arm reports null for the pruned score. `reranker` and `final` are post-ranking filters, so every returned hit clears them. A floor only removes candidates: it never widens the scope or exceeds the token budget. A floor that prunes before the limit promises no page length: pruning renumbers the survivors, and the limit and the token budget are applied afterwards, so the room a removed hit leaves can go to another hit. Every scale here is relative and never calibrated, so calibrate a cutoff against the observed scores of the same query first; a fixed cutoff can silently drop good results.

final.description: Floor on the fused score of the returned page, the same scale as scores.final. Applied to the returned set after the limit and the token budget, so it never backfills a freed slot. The floor applies to the demoted value — the fused score after `scores.age_factor` and then `scores.trust_factor` have lowered it, in that order — so a caller can predict what a floor excludes from the reported `scores.final`. Must be <= 1000000.

keyword.description: Floor on the lexical arm's raw backend score, the same scale as scores.keyword. Backend-dependent: SQLite FTS5 -bm25 and Postgres ts_rank_cd are different scales, so no cross-backend parity is claimed and one cutoff cannot be carried across backends. Must be <= 1000000.

reranker.description: Floor on the reranker's normalized relevance, the same scale as scores.reranker, 0..=1. Applied after ranking, so every returned hit clears it; a candidate the reranker did not score is kept. A value above 1 is rejected.

semantic.description: Floor on the dense arm's cosine similarity, the same scale as scores.semantic, 0..=1. Prunes the dense arm only; a value above 1 is rejected.

prefer_consolidated.description: Drop raw items whose consolidated parent is also returned; freed slots backfill.

provenance_floor.description: Weakest provenance rung the returned hits may sit at: verified (strictest, keeps facts only), stated (also keeps user_stated beliefs), third_party (also keeps third-party beliefs), inferred (loosest, keeps every rung). The ladder runs from the strictest rung to the loosest, and a hit below the floor is removed from the answer set rather than ranked lower: it is absent from the result and from co-activation reinforcement, so the floor changes set membership and nothing else — no stored field of a surviving hit moves, and no item of an excluded class is ever returned. A stricter floor promises no page length: the limit, the token budget and duplicate suppression all run after the prune, and each of them can take the room a removed hit leaves, so a floored page need not match an unfloored one in length or in ids. `dense_candidates`, `lexical_candidates` and `fused_candidates` count the candidates that survived the floor, so they read lower with a stricter floor. Omit it and the bank's own provenance_floor_default applies, and a bank that states no default means no floor. Only the four names below are accepted: any other value is rejected as invalid_argument rather than read as no floor, so a mistyped floor can never return an unfiltered page.

query_anchor.description: Optional RFC 3339 anchor (explicit UTC offset) for relative temporal expressions such as "last week"; without it the temporal arm does not run.

tools.name: retrieve

tools.description: Return the bounded context pack under the token budget. Each included hit contributes one form: flow (default) is the narrative channel and must not be the only source of a numeric or identity-bearing claim, so read `get_snapshot` for the exact stored value; exact prefers each hit's bounded rendering, charged against this same budget_tokens. A hit with no rendering contributes its gist instead; a hit with neither a rendering nor a gist is marked as a reference rather than silently replaced by its identifier, and so is a hit whose rendering did not fit the remaining budget. The pack's per-form tally counts every form.

bank.description: Isolation key; overrides the connection default when present.

fidelity.description: Which half a composed hit contributes: flow (default) packs the narrative channel, reading each hit's gist first and its bounded rendering second, and exact reads the bounded rendering first and the gist second. Only the two names below are accepted: any other value is rejected as invalid_argument rather than packed as flow, so a mistyped channel is never silently downgraded. Omit it and the bank's own pack_fidelity_default applies, and a bank that states none packs flow. A rendering is charged against the same budget_tokens as every other packed text: one that does not fit the remaining budget is dropped whole for that hit rather than shortened, and a rendering is separately bounded at 512 bytes, so a snapshot over that byte bound contributes no rendering at all. A hit whose rendering is absent contributes its gist instead; a hit with neither a rendering nor a gist is marked as a reference rather than a bare identifier, and so is a hit whose rendering did not fit the remaining budget, so the packed text and the pack's per-form tally cannot disagree.

prefer_consolidated.description: Drop raw items whose consolidated parent is also returned in the memory section.

query_anchor.description: Optional RFC 3339 anchor (explicit UTC offset) for relative temporal expressions such as "last week"; without it the temporal arm does not run.
